name: Israelites
summary: The descendants of Jacob, whom God renamed Israel: twelve tribes chosen to receive the covenant, the Law, the land of Canaan and the promise of the Messiah. Their story runs from Abraham's call through Egypt, the Exodus, the kingdoms of David and Solomon, exile and return, to Jesus of Nazareth and his Jewish apostles. The Jewish people today are their continuing descendants.
name_meaning: Israel: 'he strives with God' or 'God strives', the name given to Jacob after he wrestled at Peniel. 'Hebrew' is linked to Eber, Abraham's ancestor, or to 'one from beyond (the river)'. 'Jew' comes from Judah.

origin.account: God called Abram out of Ur and Haran with the promise 'I will make of thee a great nation… and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.' The promise passed to Isaac and then Jacob. After Jacob wrestled with God at Peniel he was named Israel, and his twelve sons became the twelve tribes. Seventy of Jacob's household went down to Egypt, where they 'increased abundantly' into a nation before the Exodus.

lineage.ancestor: Jacob (Israel), son of Isaac, son of Abraham
lineage.notes: The twelve sons of Jacob by four mothers. Leah: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun. Rachel: Joseph, Benjamin. Bilhah: Dan, Naphtali. Zilpah: Gad, Asher. Joseph's two sons Ephraim and Manasseh were adopted by Jacob as tribes. Levi received no land but became the priestly tribe, so the land was still divided among twelve. A 'mixed multitude' left Egypt with them, and outsiders such as Rahab and Ruth were grafted in.

tribes.name: Simeon
tribes.note: Scattered in Israel as Jacob foretold.

tribes.name: Levi
tribes.note: Priests and Levites; tribe of Moses and Aaron.

tribes.name: Judah

tribes.name: Issachar
tribes.note: Men 'that had understanding of the times'.

tribes.name: Zebulun
tribes.note: Named in Isaiah's 'great light' prophecy fulfilled in Jesus' Galilean ministry.

tribes.name: Dan

tribes.name: Naphtali
tribes.territory: Upper Galilee, west of the Sea of Galilee

tribes.name: Asher
tribes.note: Anna the prophetess was of Asher.

tribes.name: Joseph — Ephraim
tribes.note: Leading northern tribe; its name often stands for the whole northern kingdom.

tribes.name: Benjamin
tribes.territory: Between Judah and Ephraim, including Jerusalem's northern edge
tribes.note: Tribe of King Saul and of the apostle Paul.

homeland.region: Canaan / the land of Israel — 'from Dan even to Beer-sheba'
homeland.description: The land promised to Abraham's seed, between the Mediterranean and the Jordan, with the tribes of Reuben, Gad and half Manasseh east of the Jordan. Hill country along the centre, the coastal plain, the Jezreel Valley, Galilee in the north and the Negev in the south. Before that, Israel's ancestors came from Ur and Haran in Mesopotamia, and the nation formed in Goshen in Egypt.
homeland.modern_location: Israel, the West Bank, and parts of western Jordan and southern Lebanon and Syria.

places.name: Goshen

timeline.event: Abram leaves Haran for Canaan at God's call.
Jacob renamed Israel; his family moves to Egypt during famine through Joseph.
The Exodus from Egypt under Moses; the covenant at Sinai. 1 Kings 6:1 counts 480 years from the Exodus to Solomon's fourth year (c. 966 BC). Many scholars prefer a 13th-century date.
Wilderness wandering, then conquest and settlement of Canaan under Joshua.
Pharaoh Merneptah's victory stele names 'Israel' as a people in Canaan — the earliest mention of Israel outside the Bible.
Period of the Judges: repeated cycles of apostasy, oppression and deliverance.
United monarchy: Saul, David (who takes Jerusalem) and Solomon (who builds the Temple).
The kingdom divides: Israel (ten tribes, north) under Jeroboam and Judah (with Benjamin) under Rehoboam.
Assyria takes Samaria and deports the northern tribes.
Babylon deports Judah in stages and destroys Jerusalem and the Temple.
Cyrus of Persia allows the return; the Second Temple is completed.
Jesus of Nazareth, of the tribe of Judah and house of David, born, crucified and risen.
Rome destroys Jerusalem and the Second Temple, as Jesus foretold; the Jewish people are scattered further.

religion.practices: Worship of the one God who made heaven and earth and redeemed Israel from Egypt. Their life was shaped by the covenant Law: the Ten Commandments, sabbath, circumcision, feasts (Passover, Weeks, Tabernacles), the Tabernacle and later the Temple, priesthood and sacrifice. The prophets repeatedly called Israel back from Baal and other idols.

importance: Israel is the central people of the whole Bible. God chose them not for their size ('ye were the fewest of all people') but out of love and faithfulness to His oath. To them belong 'the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises', and from them 'as concerning the flesh Christ came'. Jesus said 'salvation is of the Jews'. The apostles and the first church were Jewish, and Paul describes Gentile believers as grafted into Israel's olive tree.

impact.how: Through Abraham's seed 'shall all the nations of the earth be blessed'; Paul applies this to the gospel going to the Gentiles.
Israel's deliverance brought the ten plagues and the Red Sea on Pharaoh's army.
Dispossessed in the conquest, a judgement the Bible ties to their own iniquity.

impact.who: Rahab, Ruth, Naaman, the widow of Zarephath
impact.how: Outsiders who came to trust Israel's God through contact with Israel.
Gentile believers are 'fellowcitizens with the saints' and heirs of Israel's promises; Paul writes that 'all Israel shall be saved'.

key_verses.text: And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing: And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.
And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed.

For thou art an holy people unto the LORD thy God: the LORD thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth. The LORD did not set his love upon you, nor choose you, because ye were more in number than any people; for ye were the fewest of all people: But because the LORD loved you, and because he would keep the oath which he had sworn unto your fathers, hath the LORD brought you out with a mighty hand, and redeemed you out of the house of bondmen, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
Ye worship ye know not what: we know what we worship: for salvation is of the Jews.

Who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises; Whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen.

fate.summary: Israel was never wiped out. The northern tribes were scattered by Assyria, though members of all tribes had earlier moved south to Judah (2 Chronicles 11:16; 15:9), and Anna of Asher was still identified by her tribe in Jesus' day. Judah returned from Babylon, lived under Persian, Greek and Roman rule, and was scattered again after AD 70 and AD 135. In AD 1948 the modern State of Israel was established.

today.summary: The Jewish people are the living continuation of biblical Israel — about 15.8 million worldwide (2025 estimate, Sergio DellaPergola / Jewish Agency), roughly half in the State of Israel and most of the rest in the United States. Samaritans also claim descent from the northern tribes. Some other communities, such as Ethiopia's Beta Israel and India's Bnei Menashe, hold traditions of descent from the 'lost' tribes.
today.descendants: Ashkenazi, Sephardi, Mizrahi and other Jewish communities worldwide; the Samaritans (see samaritans).
today.modern_legacy: The Hebrew Bible (Christians' Old Testament), Hebrew as a living language, the synagogue, the sabbath, and the ethical monotheism shared by Judaism, Christianity and Islam.

archaeology.name: Merneptah Stele
archaeology.significance: 'Israel is laid waste, his seed is not' — the earliest mention of Israel outside the Bible, as a people in Canaan.

archaeology.name: Tel Dan Stele
archaeology.significance: An Aramean king boasts of victory over the 'king of Israel' and the 'house of David' — the first certain mention of David outside the Bible.

archaeology.name: Black Obelisk of Shalmaneser III
archaeology.significance: Shows 'Jehu son of Omri' (or his envoy) bowing before the Assyrian king.

archaeology.name: Siloam Tunnel inscription
archaeology.significance: Records the digging of Hezekiah's tunnel.

archaeology.name: Ketef Hinnom silver scrolls
archaeology.significance: Carry the priestly blessing — the oldest known text also found in the Bible.
